% metadata — the document information dictionary, read into YAML frontmatter.
%
% One concern: does "md -frontmatter" report what the file says about itself? Every
% other fixture here asserts the prose and is built with the frontmatter off, so
% nothing on disk looked at that output at all — which is half of why the object
% layer dropped /Info for the project's whole life and no test failed. The other
% half was a test that walked the emitted lines without counting them.
%
% This is the only fixture that sets any of Title, Author, Subject or Keywords.
% None of the other nine do, so the four fields most likely to be wrong were also
% the four that no expectation covered. LaTeX does not write \title into /Info on
% its own — that is hyperref's job, via \hypersetup — so the absence was a property
% of the sources rather than of the engine.
%
% The title carries a colon and the keywords a comma on purpose. "ISO 32000-2:
% Document management" is the real case sink/markdown's quoting rule names, and a
% ": " anywhere in a value ends a YAML key, so the gold file asserts the quoted form
% rather than the plain one. The comma is the counter-example beside it: it needs no
% quoting outside a flow collection, so a rule that quoted defensively on any
% punctuation would fail here and be visible.
%
% lang comes from the catalogue's /Lang and not from /Info, which is why it is set
% separately. It is the one frontmatter field with a different source, so a fixture
% that only exercised /Info would leave the two indistinguishable.
%
% hidelinks because hyperref's default is a coloured border around every link, and
% this document has no links to draw one on — the option keeps the page identical to
% what it would be without the package so the body assertion stays about the prose.
%
% \pdfinfo overrides /ModDate to a value that is not the build time, which pdfTeX
% honours while still writing its own /CreationDate. That makes the two dates
% different, and the difference is the assertion: with both equal, a reader that
% filled Modified from /CreationDate emitted a plausible value that matched, and the
% mutation survived the whole suite. A fixed date rather than a second timestamp
% because the point is that we return what the file says, and a value nobody's clock
% produced cannot be arrived at by accident.
%
% Build with pdflatex; nothing here needs the tagging backend.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
\pdfinfo{/ModDate (D:20240131120000Z)}
\hypersetup{
  pdftitle={Metadata: a reference fixture},
  pdfauthor={A. Author},
  pdfsubject={The fields an information dictionary carries},
  pdfkeywords={pdf, metadata, frontmatter},
  pdflang={en},
}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}

This document exists for what its information dictionary says, not for what its page
draws.

\end{document}
